audit.why: Both layers read 'Skill' on all seven rows and agree with each other, and the kits support it: two immobile mages whose openers are both hard-CC skillshots (Light Binding 1175, Sleepy Trouble Bubble 800), neither with a lane-flipping cooldown edge. Lux's 53.7% comes from range, not from a stage she owns outright, so I did not move any row.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text described Lux's R as a 'skillshot snare-finisher' — Final Spark does not snare — and never named Portal Jump.
audit.why: Final Spark is a 3340-range damage beam that refreshes Illumination; it applies no CC. Zoe's R is Portal Jump, an 11/8/5s blink out and back, which is why level 6 adds no hard all-in for her either.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text now names Final Spark's range and Portal Jump's cooldown as the reason 6 stays even.

audit.whatIsWrong: Q was written as 'Paddle Star' (packet suspectName, distance 1) instead of Paddle Star!; breakdown.cooldowns had no digit; the More Sparkles! auto-reset tell was absent.
audit.why: Sleepy Trouble Bubble 18/17/16/15/14s reduces MR while asleep and DOUBLES the first source of damage that breaks the sleep, up to a cap — so the shield goes on the wake-up hit, not the poke. Paddle Star! is 8.5/8/7.5/7/6.5s and deals more damage the longer it flies straight, so breaking its line or closing distance cuts it. Portal Jump falls to 5s at rank 3. More Sparkles! empowers her next auto after any cast.
audit.corrected: Name fixed to Paddle Star!; cooldowns field rebuilt with all three real numbers; dosFull[1].d carries the More Sparkles! wind-up tell and the doubled wake-up damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The missing-interactions file claims Sleepy Trouble Bubble creates terrain that cuts your retreat, and the kit carries trueDamage and terrain flags on it.
audit.why: Riot's own text for Sleepy Trouble Bubble describes drowsiness, sleep, reduced Magic Resist and doubled break damage — no terrain and no true damage. Both flags contradict the description, so I trusted the description and wrote neither onto the page.

edits.before: Pure skillshot duel: whoever lands their setup wins. Your Bind roots for her E-Q, but her E (Sleepy Trouble Bubble) into Q (Paddle Star) does the same to you, so it's a mirror of sidesteps.
edits.after: Pure skillshot duel: whoever lands their setup wins. Your Bind roots for her E-Q, but her E (Sleepy Trouble Bubble) into Q (Paddle Star!) does the same to you, so it's a mirror of sidesteps.

edits.before: Both of you gain a range/utility spike but no hard all-in swing: your R is a skillshot snare-finisher, her Sleep plus double-Q burst is a coin flip on who dodges first.
edits.after: Both gain a spike without a hard all-in swing: Final Spark is a 3340-range finisher, and Portal Jump is an 11s blink she uses to fire Paddle Star! and vanish.

edits.before: - Zoe Sleepy Trouble Bubble: matchup-defining — Sleep into empowered Q is the entire kill pattern — body-block it with minions or terrain. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Prismatic Barrier like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sleepy Trouble Bubble is 18s at rank 1 and 14s maxed — that whole window is your walk-up time. - Paddle Star! is 8.5s early and hits harder the longer it flies, so close the gap or break the line. - Portal Jump is only 5s late, so she blinks out of your Q on repeat.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: More Sparkles! empowers her auto after a cast — that wind-up is the tell; shield the doubled damage that breaks the sleep, not the poke.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Light Binding is your only answer to her step-up, and at 10s it is the slowest thing in your kit — spend it on her commit, not on spacing.

edits.before: Zoe wins by landing Sleepy Trouble Bubble, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Zoe wins by landing Sleepy Trouble Bubble from fog, doubling the first damage that wakes you, and blinking away on Portal Jump.

edits.before: Ahead, own the geometry: E Zoe off every contact, root the answers, and laser the river fights from fog — fed Lux turns vision lines into kill lines.
edits.after: Ahead, take her walk-up: Sleepy Trouble Bubble is 18s early, so every whiffed bubble is a free window to E the wave, root her, and take a plate.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by winning the fog war: your R reaches 3340 and her bubble only 800, so fights you open from vision she cannot answer without walking in.

notes: Chart left untouched — both layers already agree on 'Skill' across all seven rows and the kits support an even lane, so there was nothing to reconcile. Zoe's kit carries trueDamage and terrain flags on Sleepy Trouble Bubble that contradict Riot's own description (sleep, reduced MR, doubled break damage); I trusted the description and did not write terrain-blocks-retreat or true-damage advice, even though _missing key 29 asks for both. Whether Cleanse or tenacity affects the drowsy/sleep is not in the kit text and was not asserted.
